sections.html:
Clarkstown is the most densely populated town in Rockland County, on the county's eastern edge with the Hudson River as its boundary. It covers about 47 square miles, and the 2020 census counted 86,855 residents. The hamlet of New City is the county seat and the seat of town government, and about 41 percent of the town's people live there.

The town also holds Bardonia, Congers, Central Nyack, Nanuet, Valley Cottage, West Nyack, Rockland Lake, Mount Ivy, the village of Upper Nyack, and the eastern part of the village of Spring Valley. Commuters use the Thruway (I-87 and I-287) and the Palisades Interstate Parkway, NJ Transit's Pascack Valley Line at Nanuet, and Rockland Coaches express buses to the Port Authority Bus Terminal.

Several districts divide the town, so the address matters. The Clarkstown Central School District serves most of it, including New City, Bardonia, Congers and West Nyack. Nyack Public Schools serve Upper Nyack, Valley Cottage and Central Nyack, the Nanuet Union Free School District serves Nanuet, and a small slice on the western border belongs to East Ramapo.

Quote the district from the tax bill, since one street can sit in a different district from the next.

Clarkstown's Town Clerk, at 10 Maple Avenue in New City, collects town and county property tax for a calendar year. Full payment is due by January 31 with no penalty. Late charges and the quarterly option are in the schedule below.

Payment choiceDate or windowCharge
Full payment, no penaltyBy January 31None
Full paymentFebruary 1 to 28Additional 1%
Full paymentMarch 1 to 31Additional 2%
Quarterly paymentsJanuary 15, April 15, July 15, October 155% service charge
School tax, full paymentBy September 30None
School tax, lateOctober 1 to 31Additional 5%

The second to fourth quarterly installments are payable to Rockland County Budget and Finance in Pomona. No official can waive a statutory penalty, and a missing bill does not change what is owed. If no bill arrives in the first week of January or September, call the office for a duplicate.

sections.h2: What is on a Clarkstown tax bill
sections.html:
The bill is a line-by-line list: county tax, town tax, an open space charge, fire district, water district, lighting district, sewer, refuse, ambulance and charges set by Rockland Green. A one, two or three family house counts as homestead, and anything larger counts as non-homestead. Fire districts vary, so two Clarkstown neighbors can pay different amounts.

When you sell, the closing attorney prorates the bill between you and the buyer. Have the most recent bill in hand at the first meeting, along with proof of any amount already paid. If a quarterly installment is still open, the payoff comes out of your proceeds, and a cash buyer can close around that without waiting on a lender.

The July 1 before a roll is the valuation date, and all properties are valued at market conditions on that date. March 1 is the taxable status date, when ownership and condition are fixed and exemption applications must reach the Assessor. The tentative roll is filed May 1, which opens the formal grievance period. Grievance Day is the fourth Tuesday in May, when the Board of Assessment Review hears complaints and every application must be on file. The 2027 date is May 25.

Timing matters for a seller. A house sold in December still carries the status it had on March 1, and the next roll uses the next July 1 valuation. If you think the tentative figure is too high, collect comparable sales and photographs before May. The town posts an online property assessment search for checking your record.

A Certificate of Occupancy is the town's assurance to a prospective buyer that a building is legally occupied and meets zoning and minimum repair and maintenance standards as of the issue date. One is required for an initial occupation, an alteration of an existing building, a change in use, or whenever a building permit has been issued. No certificate is issued while a deficiency or material violation remains uncorrected.

  • An altered, extended or enlarged building may not be used for more than 30 days after completion without a certificate.
  • A temporary certificate can be issued for a building in full compliance with zoning and near compliance with other rules, and it expires in 90 days.
  • Buildings that predate zoning and building codes, or permits that expired, carry an additional fee.
  • You apply at the Building Department, Room 101 on the lower level of Town Hall, 10 Maple Avenue.

Clarkstown does not require fence permits, but zoning limits residential solid fences and walls to 4 and a half feet along any lot line, and caps other fences at 6 feet unless they are set back from the lot line. Wood stoves and fireplaces always need a building permit. Ask the Building Department what is on file for your address before you list.

If the house has tenants, the town's Rental Registry Law applies. Every owner of a one-family or two-family dwelling who rents it must register with the Building Department, unless the owner lives there. An approved registration lasts two years, and the town inspects registered rentals every two years, including smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and fire extinguishers.

Brokers must verify that a current rental registration exists before they list, show or offer a registered dwelling unit for lease, rent or sale. Penalties start at $4,500 to $6,000 for a first offense and rise for repeat offenses, with a separate weekly fine for each week a violation continues. If you inherited a rented house, ask the Building Department whether it is registered before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: Recording the deed in Rockland County
sections.html:
The Rockland County Clerk records deeds, mortgages and satisfactions for Clarkstown. Documents must be originals in recordable form, legible, signed and notarized. The clerk charges a $45 filing fee and $5 per page, plus a $10 notification fee for deed filings and the current fees for the TP-584 and RP-5217 forms.

State law sets transfer tax at $2 for each $500 of price, paid by the seller, and the TP-584 is due within 15 days of delivering the deed. A 1 percent mansion tax is owed by the buyer on residences of $1 million or more. Ask your closing attorney early about the title search and the deed form, since a cash sale is recorded the same way as a financed one.

faqs.q: How many people live in Clarkstown, NY?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 86,855 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 89,659. New City makes up about 41 percent of the town.

faqs.q: When are Clarkstown town and county taxes due?
faqs.a: Full payment is due January 31 without penalty, with 1 percent added in February and 2 percent in March. The quarterly plan adds a 5 percent service charge and has installments on January 15, April 15, July 15 and October 15.

faqs.q: Does Clarkstown require a certificate of occupancy to sell a house?
faqs.a: The town requires one for new occupancy, alterations, a change in use, or when a building permit was issued. Ask the Building Department what is on file for your address before you list.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a rental house in Clarkstown?
faqs.a: Yes, if you own a one or two-family dwelling and rent it out without living there. Registration lasts two years and the town inspects rentals every two years.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in Clarkstown?
faqs.a: It is the fourth Tuesday in May, the day the Board of Assessment Review hears complaints on the May 1 tentative roll. The 2027 date is May 25.
